answer_markdown:
**Short answer:** For land acquisition proceedings to lapse under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, it must be established that neither the possession of the land has been taken nor the compensation has been paid, and this lapse must occur due to the inaction of the authorities for five years or more prior to the commencement of the Act [S7][S8].

**What the sources say:**
* The Supreme Court held that the word “or” in Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act should be read as “nor” or as “and” [S7].
* The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act occurs where, due to the inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to the commencement of the Act, "the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid" [S7].
* The Supreme Court stated that "twin conditions, of not taking over the possession and not paying / tendering the compensation, are required to be satisfied" for the lapsing of the acquisition under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 [S8].
* The Court observed that if one of the conditions is not satisfied, there shall not be deemed lapse of the acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 [S8].
* The Court noted that in case possession has been taken, but compensation has not been paid, there is no lapse, and similarly, if compensation has been paid, but possession has not been taken, there is no lapse [S7].
* The Supreme Court also stated that if the award has been passed within the window period of five years excluding the period covered by an interim order of the court, then proceedings shall continue as provided under Section 24(1)(b) of the 2013 Act under the 1894 Act as if it has not been repealed [S6][S7][S8].

**How it may apply:**
* The lapse is provided only in case of default by Authorities acquiring the land, and not caused by any other reason or order of the court [S1].
* The period of five years is provided for authorities to take action, not to "sleep over the matter" [S1].
* The period of stay granted in favour of landowners ought to be excluded when considering the five-year period under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act [S5].

**Uncertain or not covered:** The sources do not specify the exact facts that must be present for the lapse to occur, other than the two conditions regarding possession and compensation, and the five-year period of inaction by the authorities [S7][S8].

**Jurisdiction and date:** Supreme Court of India judgments; based on texts retrieved on 2026-09-22.
